header: Date: 2027-07-07 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Redwood AE+SE (Jordan, Maya), Product (Liam) — Aurora HealthTech (Sofia, Ethan, Priya, Carlos)
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on cache priming signals and KV cache hit-rate improvements. Reviewed last weeks' metric trends (KV hit + session reuse), discussed signal tuning approach (session score, entropy thresholds), and agreed on a staged test: 24h headroom run, slight eviction leniency, and expanded tracing. Security asked clarifying Qs re: PII retention and audit logs. Next steps and owners captured.
topics: Prompt reuse vs full regen tradeoffs
transcript: 00:00 Sofia Ramos: okay we can start — sorry running a bit late everyone
00:08 Jordan Ellis: no worries, thanks for making time. we're gonna go through the cache priming tuning and the metrics from last week
00:16 Maya Patel: quick agenda: 1) metrics recap 2) proposed signal change 3) small experiment plan 4) security/ops questions
00:30 Ethan Park: sounds good. we've got staging dashboards up, they'll be read-only for you today
00:39 Jordan Ellis: perfect — Liam are you on the perf numbers?
00:44 Liam O'Connor: yeah I pulled the rolling seven-day; main takeaway is kv hit climbed from ~21% to 33% after the cohort rule, but we saw tail latency spikes around  p95 for some sessions
00:58 Sofia Ramos: yep that matches what we saw — the e2e latency p95 jumped when we had heavy multipart prompts

01:09 Maya Patel: right, the multipart prompts are killing the prefix matcher because prefix length variance is high, so cache priming score needs to favor structural similarity not just string prefix
01:22 Priya Mehta: can you explain structural similarity? is that like embeddings?
01:26 Maya Patel: yeah similar idea — lightweight fingerprinting, not full embed; we compute a session signature from intents+slot keys, that pushes reuse for templated prompts
01:39 Carlos Ruiz: security question — when you fingerprint session data is that PII? we need to be sure that hashing isn't reversible and that no raw prompt text is persisted beyond TTL

01:53 Jordan Ellis: good call — short answer: our runtime stores only salted hashes of the fingerprint and we never persist raw text to long-term storage, TTLs are configurable and logs can be scrubbed
02:06 Carlos Ruiz: okay please include that in the security doc you promised last week, we need it for the audit
02:11 Jordan Ellis: noted, will include salt details and retention window in the doc

02:17 Maya Patel: back to hit-rate: we proposed adding an entropy threshold so we don't prime very high-entropy generative prompts. that raised hit-rate to ~38% in canary for certain cohorts without raising bad outputs
02:36 Ethan Park: can you remind us what the entropy threshold was?
02:40 Maya Patel: we used a simple token-entropy heuristic, threshold around 4.2 on our lightweight scorer — it's coarse but cheap
02:50 Sofia Ramos: in staging though we saw a small increase in hallucination rate for customer-support prompts when threshold was too lenient
02:59 Liam O'Connor: correct — the recall improved but precision of relevant prefix dropped slightly; we can mitigate by mixing in prompt-level signals like 'is structured template'
03:12 Priya Mehta: is there a tradeoff with quantization? I remember last month some degraded scoring when we switched q4_kv kernel
03:19 Maya Patel: good point — kernel quantization can change tokenization nuances and affect the fingerprint. we recommend running a calibration pass after quantization changes
03:30 Jordan Ellis: action item: Maya will run a 24h headroom test that ramps the entropy threshold up and down and records KV hit, p50/p95 latency, and failure rates
03:42 Maya Patel: yep and I'll share the raw traces and aggregated pivot table — should be done by Monday 2027-07-12
03:52 Sofia Ramos: can you also include an experiment toggling eviction leniency? we think our small sessions are getting evicted too fast
04:00 Maya Patel: sure — we'll do two lanes: current eviction policy (baseline) and lenient + session-score aging. compare hit-rate and memory footprint
04:12 Ethan Park: memory footprint is key, we only have 48GB of kv per pod in staging so headroom test needs caps
04:20 Liam O'Connor: we'll set caps and also try soft-evict: keep sessions beyond TTL for X minutes but mark them for lower-priority eviction
04:32 Priya Mehta: does Redwood support session-affinity routing? we want to bias requests to warmed pods
04:38 Jordan Ellis: yes, can route by session-id affinity; we can add a weighted sticky policy for 5–10 minutes to improve local cache reuse
04:48 Carlos Ruiz: remember we have compliance constraints — session affinity must respect our SSO session boundaries and log everything
04:56 Jordan Ellis: we'll map affinity TTL to your SSO session expiry, and include audit log lines for routing decisions
05:05 Sofia Ramos: quick sanity question — are we using prefix reuse or full prompt reuse for templated messages? sometimes reuse yields stale placeholders

05:14 Maya Patel: we have two modes: prefix reuse (replay initial KV for later tokens) and full prompt reuse (re-supply prior completed output). template mode uses placeholders + post-fill to avoid stale slots
05:28 Sofia Ramos: hmm we've seen slot mismatch when users change context mid-session — does the priming logic check recency of slot values?
05:36 Maya Patel: yes session fingerprint includes last-updated timestamps per slot; we only reuse if slot recency < Y minutes and hash matches
05:46 Ethan Park: what's Y?
05:48 Maya Patel: default 15 minutes, but adjustable per-customer
05:53 Priya Mehta: so for Aurora we may want Y=10 because content changes faster in our product
05:58 Jordan Ellis: we can make that a pilot variable — Maya will include it in the matrix
06:03 Liam O'Connor: another datapoint: when we increased cohort size the hit-rate increased but network egress grew a bit due to more cross-pod prefetching
06:12 Maya Patel: that's the trade-off: aggressive priming increases kv reads and cross-pod transfers. that's why headroom test will track egress and cost delta
06:21 Sofia Ramos: on the cost note — Jordan can you run two pricing scenarios for the pilot: baseline vs lenient-evict? we need to show execs
06:29 Jordan Ellis: yes I'll include a 30-day extrapolated delta with cost per kv-read and estimated savings from reduced tokens
06:36 Carlos Ruiz: we also want to know log retention impact. if you increase tracing for headroom we'll need a retention plan and maybe a separate bucket
06:45 Maya Patel: we can stream detailed traces to a short-lived bucket and aggregate metrics to the main dashboard; raw traces auto-delete after 14 days unless you ask otherwise
06:55 Sofia Ramos: that should be fine, we just need the retention configs in writing
07:02 Jordan Ellis: will include in security doc. question from our side: any blockers to granting read-only dashboard access?
07:09 Ethan Park: we can provision a role by tomorrow, but need an IP allowlist for the AE account
07:15 Jordan Ellis: will provide IPs — thanks
07:19 Priya Mehta: quick thought: could Redwood do a classifier to skip priming for low-value queries? we have a lot of "what is my plan" queries that are free-form
07:29 Maya Patel: yes that's basically what the entropy and template signal combo does; we can also add a cheap intent classifier as another gating signal
07:36 Sofia Ramos: any guidance on thresholds? we don't want to blow the hit-rate with false negatives
07:42 Liam O'Connor: empirical approach — start conservative: only prime for high template-confidence > 0.8 and entropy < 3.8, then relax in lanes
07:54 Maya Patel: we'll include those lanes in the experiment matrix
08:00 Carlos Ruiz: on encryption — KMS for in-flight cache isn't possible obviously but at-rest keys must be customer-managed for private deployment; we need confirmation
08:10 Jordan Ellis: for Private we support customer-managed KMS; for hosted pilot we can offer bring-your-own-KMS on a restricted basis, we'll note specifics in the security doc
08:20 Sofia Ramos: timeline recap please?

08:23 Jordan Ellis: sure: Maya runs 24h headroom + eviction leniency lanes and shares results by 2027-07-12; Jordan sends pricing and pilot extension by 2027-07-09; Aurora provides staging dashboard access and sample traces by 2027-07-10
08:36 Priya Mehta: that works. any blockers on our end we should call out?
08:40 Ethan Park: need to check network egress limits, might request a temporary quota bump for the test window
08:46 Jordan Ellis: understood — include quota request in the reply thread and we'll coordinate with infra
08:50 Maya Patel: one more technical note — we'll instrument a small canary to validate that fingerprinting is stable across quant kernels; if unstable we'll pin kernel per-pod for the pilot
09:02 Sofia Ramos: good idea. the last time quant drifted we had weird cache misses
09:08 Jordan Ellis: okay final check: any objections to the plan?
09:12 Priya Mehta: none from product
09:14 Carlos Ruiz: just get that security doc and retention config in writing and we're good
09:18 Sofia Ramos: thanks everyone, appreciate the deep dive
09:22 Jordan Ellis: thanks team — we'll follow up in the thread with artifacts. Maya will post the experiment matrix and a short runbook
09:29 Maya Patel: I'll include the matrix, pivot tables, and a small troubleshooting checklist
09:34 Jordan Ellis: perfect. meeting adjourned — 45 minutes on the clock. bye
09:38 (call ends)
